summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of multiple sclerosis, ulcerative colitis, and asthma was readmitted for her second dose of methotrexate chemotherapy for primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. She reported new-onset numbness and tingling in her right foot that had extended up the lateral leg. Evaluation included a negative lower extremity ultrasound for DVT and a spine MRI that showed no leptomeningeal spread of lymphoma but revealed degenerative changes at L3-4. Symptoms were likely related to either MS or nerve root irritation, and she was started on gabapentin. Her methotrexate was administered without complication, though transaminitis developed, presumed to be drug-related. She was managed with leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, which were continued post-discharge. Dexamethasone was tapered, omeprazole was switched to ranitidine, and Dilaudid was discontinued. She remained stable, was discharged home, and will return in two weeks for port placement and next-cycle chemotherapy.
